---
title: Replicate This Study
description: Everything you need to run this evaluation yourself — with your own models, annotators, or question bank extensions.
---

All materials needed to replicate this evaluation are published openly. This page describes what you need, what you can reuse as-is, and where adaptation may be required.

## What You Need

1. **API access** to the models you want to evaluate — a single OpenRouter key covers all six used here. See [Data Collection](../data-collection/index.qmd) for setup.
2. **Python 3.10+** and the packages listed in [Environment Setup](../data-collection/setup.qmd).
3. **At least two annotators** who have read the primary and secondary literature for the figures under evaluation. See [Annotation Protocol](../methodology/index.qmd#annotation-protocol) for how ours were prepared and what that trade-off costs.
4. **The rubric and scoring sheet** — see [The Rubric](../methodology/index.qmd#the-rubric).
5. **The question bank** — download from [Figures & Question Bank](../figures/index.qmd).

## What You Can Reuse Without Modification

- The full question bank (11 general questions per figure plus 6–7 figure-specific ones, [CSV](../figures/question_bank.csv))
- The rubric definitions and scoring sheet template ([The Rubric](../methodology/index.qmd#the-rubric))
- The collection pipeline and response format ([Data Collection](../data-collection/index.qmd))
- The annotation protocol ([Annotation Protocol](../methodology/index.qmd#annotation-protocol))
- The reference profiles and fact-check sheets for each figure, published in condensed form on the figure pages ([Macrina](../figures/macrina.qmd), [Olympias](../figures/olympias.qmd))

## What May Require Adaptation

- **New models**: add the model's pinned version string to the collection script. Temperature 0 and the verbatim prompt text should be used unchanged for comparability.
- **New figures**: add a page to the Figures section following the template of [Macrina the Younger](../figures/macrina.qmd), ask the 11 general questions with the figure's name substituted, and write 6–7 figure-specific questions — including at least one built on a false premise the record does not support.
- **Different annotators**: build your own reference profile and fact-check sheet before scoring, and report inter-annotator agreement per dimension alongside any results — alpha together with raw exact and within-one-point agreement, since alpha alone can mislead when scores are concentrated.

## Citing This Work

If you use the question bank, rubric, or methodology from this project, please cite:

> Araujo, Eric; Rylaarsdam, D.; Holtrop, Nathan; Hawthorne, Ian. *Matristics: LLM Evaluation in Early Church History*. 2026.
